summary: A set of measurements of how fast a TENEX host could send data over the ARPANET. The author wrote a simple program that sent strings to itself and counted throughput, then tabulated results for different byte sizes. It reports real baud rate and the share of CPU used.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reports measurements from a TENEX program that sent data to itself over the network. The tables compare throughput and CPU use for different byte sizes and transfer modes.

questions: what bandwidth did tenex achieve in the tests
how did buffered and unbuffered transfer differ
how much cpu did network transfers use
subtitle: A TENEX test of network throughput and the CPU used for transfers.

tldr.problem: The author wanted to examine TENEX host performance during network transfers, rather than calculate transfer costs.
tldr.mechanism: A simple program sent strings to itself over the network and counted throughput and CPU use for different byte sizes and transfer modes.
tldr.outcome: The tables show different real and CPU baud rates for buffered and unbuffered transfers under the reported test conditions.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 415 as Unknown and records no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. The RFC reports TENEX performance measurements under specified test conditions.

sections.title: Test Setup
sections.content:
The author describes a simple TENEX program that sent strings over the network to itself, using BIN/BOUT and buffered send mode. It counted data but did not process the strings. Samples contained one million bits.

The tests ran with no other load on the system, using an early version of TENEX 1.29. Input and output halves were averaged together, so reported baud rates used two million bits of combined traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: The test program sent data out and received it back without processing the contents. The reported rates combine the outgoing and returning data.

sections.title: Buffered Transfer Results
sections.content:
With buffered send mode and 36-bit sizes, the table reports real baud rates from 46.5K to 61.1K and CPU baud rates from 267K to 322K. CPU needed ranges from 15% to 22% for those entries.

With buffered send mode and 8-bit sizes, real baud rates range from 22.0K to 41.8K, while CPU needed ranges from 31% to 70%. The table lists each tested byte size separately.
sections.plainLanguage: The buffered tests report different speeds and CPU use for different byte sizes. The values are measurements under the stated test conditions, not a guarantee for other systems.

sections.title: Unbuffered Transfers and Other Comparisons
sections.content:
The second table uses SIN/SOUT without buffered mode. For 36-bit sizes, its real baud rates range from 36K to 54K and CPU needed ranges from 38% to 60%. For 8-bit sizes, real baud rates range from 12K to 20K and CPU needed ranges from 57% to 99%.

The RFC also reports that TTYs and line printers have ultimate CPU bandwidths near 15-20 KB, and that a TIP tape transmission using NETMAG was about 7 kilobits per second and used about 30% of the CPU.
sections.plainLanguage: The unbuffered table reports its own speeds and CPU use for each size. The RFC also gives comparison figures for local terminals, printers and a tape transfer.

references.text: RFC 392, which the author cites as a discussion of network-use cost.
